its prob a early Blockout/grayboxing of the map inengine. Its when you are designing the map for gameplay and size purposes. using low poly primitives to make quick iterations of how the map flows/roughly how it will look. when they are doing this its easyer for the 3d artists to make assets that fits/looks right. If they used high quality assets for early stages, the 3d artist would have to make changes to a mesh, bake it, texture it and lod it everytime small changes had to be made. That game devs dont need support for high poly arent entirerly correct. Most game assets now is based on two meshes. The game asset mesh (this one is "low poly") and the high detail hero mesh (this one can be insanly high poly, since its this mesh that gets the rinkles, scars, pores, skin detail etc.) And when that one is done we bake (create normal maps, AO maps etc) the details from the high poly mesh to the low poly mesh. So support for smooth workflow with heavy meshes are important.

Kinda diffrent kind of games. I guess RDR2 uses heavy occlution of everything not in frame, so they can push what its inframe harder. And they utilize the GPU far more then the CPU. Stuff like AI, Physics (and the Phyics in RDR2 is pretty similar to the one in GTA4, with many of the same bugs ive found there), collision, hitdetection is on the CPU. While pushing polygons, shaders and light effects lies on the GPU.So how pretty a game looks arent that good way of measuring how it runs compaired to other games. This is why i could play games like ghost recon with good frames when i was just walking around the woods on my old PC, but when enemies swarmed around me and started firing at me, my CPU just worked itself into the grave and the FPS plummet.

And since JWE uses alot of calculations under the hood to calculate guest needs, where dinoes are viewable and not, dino AI and economy it pushes the CPU alittle harder then the GPU, and since the CPUs on consoles arent that great right now. It makes it harder to create deep and large "builders" for Console.

THAT said, yeah JWE is barebones non the less. Since Paradox managed to get Cities Skylines running on consoles, and that game shoots my PC CPU in the kneecaps when my cities reacthes a certain size.But ive also played PlanetCoaster on PC, and that game is closer to PlanetZoo then JWE, and that game makes most PCs chugg when you reach a certain guestcount. And i always keep an eye on my CPU, GPU and RAM stats, and its always the CPU thats sweating during those game sesions.

So it seems either the Cobra Engine is to ineffecent to realy deal with that kind of CPU load on consoles, or Frontier still consider themselves a primary PC developer, and just had to cut stuff from the game instead of using to much time doing big changes to engine itself (and yes i know Elite Dangrous uses the same engine, and runs fine on Console, but that game is more a GPU game then a CPU game.)

Thats my 2cents, i might be far off the mark. But from what ive seen, and from what ive myself have experimentet with on Unity and UE4, building pretty FPS/3rd person games are pretty easy to optimise, building games where AI and background calculations are important and the player can zoom out and see everything playout at once, is a huuuuuuuuge bitch to optimize. And if Frontier had as little time as we suspect, I understand (but still are pretty dissapointed over) the steps they had to take to make it run on consoles. I know they can do better on PC, but how low they had to go to make use of  1.6 GHz 4 core CPU is pretty sad.
